title.narrative: Emergency Response to Flood-Affected Communities in Adamawa State, Nigeria

description.narrative: The recent flooding in Adamawa State has displaced over 10,000 people, destroying homes, farmland, and essential infrastructure. Communities have lost food stocks and livelihoods, with many households now sheltering in overcrowded temporary sites without access to safe water and adequate sanitation, thereby increasing the risk of cholera and other waterborne diseases (Adamawa SEMA, Local Government Assessments, Aug 2025). Vulnerable groups, including women, children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, face heightened protection risks, including exposure to gender-based violence. This project will deliver a coordinated, multi-sectoral emergency response over 45 days, reaching 10,000 individuals (1,667 households) in the worst-affected communities. Activities include: Unconditional cash transfers to enable affected households to meet immediate food needs and restore basic livelihoods and enhance protection environment. The approach integrates protection mainstreaming, disability inclusion, and accountability to affected populations through feedback mechanisms by addressing urgent needs for shelter, water, and food while enabling households to recover basic means of survival, the project will reduce immediate suffering and contribute to community resilience during the critical recovery period. The project seeks to deliver life-saving emergency assistance severely impacted by recent flooding in Yola. The project is expected to meet critical needs quickly, reduce vulnerability, and contribute to restoring dignity among affected households.
